objective: Have the Go implementation preserve supported TypeScript behavior and make additional source providers easy to support.
policy: Preserve functionality and supported outputs; do not reproduce TypeScript bugs. Production cutover and shipping a new external provider are separate from implementation parity.

intentionalDifferences: Invalid resource options return 400 without partial database writes.
Structured JSON errors replace framework-generated HTML parser errors.
Resource bounds, cancellation and credential isolation remain enforced.
operationalLimits: No production data or production deployment changed.
Production restore/queue handoff/rollback requires a separate target-data rehearsal.
Live private-repository revocation and suspension are not proven by public beta tests; automated protocol tests cover these controls.
No GitLab or Bitbucket adapter shipped. New adapters need their own provider-specific credential connection flow.
Performance measurements describe recorded workloads, not an overall production speedup.

firstFullRace.cause: Shared TestBackendIntegration context expired at five minutes after expanded provider lifecycle checks. Subsequent DB operations failed with context deadline exceeded.
firstFullRace.fix: Use the Go test runner deadline, reserving five seconds for cleanup. Application deadlines unchanged.

interruptedFullRace.cause: SIGTERM; process confirmed terminal and disposable services removed. No completed test result.

source.algorithm: SHA-256 over sorted backend-relative path, NUL, file bytes, NUL; Go sources, go.mod and go.sum

conclusion: Supported TypeScript functionality and outputs are implemented and verified under the documented compatibility policy. Shared provider interfaces and non-GitHub lifecycle coverage satisfy the provider extension requirement. No implementation requirement remains open; production cutover limits are listed separately.
